title: Yosef Meshita
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A wondrous story is told about him in Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 65, section 22 (which Hyman places in the days of the Greeks, before the Hasmoneans arose). The enemies wanted to enter the Temple Mount and said: let one of the Jews enter first, and they told him that whatever he brought out first he could keep for himself. Yosef Meshita entered and brought out a golden menorah. They said to him: it is not the way of a commoner to use this; but if you enter a second time, then whatever you bring out you may take for yourself. Then he contemplated repentance in his heart and did not want to enter a second time. They promised him the tax revenue of three years, but he did not accept it, and said: Is it not enough that I angered my God once, that I should anger Him a second time? And they inflicted great torments on him and put him into a carpenters' (saw) frame, and they sawed him. But he sanctified the Name of Heaven and cried out: Woe that I angered my Creator! May his memory be blessed.

notes.text: The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 65:22 contains Yosef Meshita’s menorah, refusal, three-year tax offer and saw-frame narrative. Hyman’s Greek and pre-Hasmonean dating is not stated in that directly consulted locus. The following Yakum story is separate.
